attractions.name: Sukkur Barrage
attractions.description: A major British-era irrigation barrage on the Indus River, an engineering landmark feeding Sindh's canal network.

attractions.name: Sadhu Bela Temple
attractions.description: A Hindu temple complex located on an island in the Indus River, accessible by boat.

attractions.name: Lansdowne Bridge
attractions.description: A historic cantilever bridge over the Indus River, an important piece of colonial-era engineering.

attractions.name: Mohenjo-daro (day trip)
attractions.description: One of the world's oldest urban archaeological sites from the Indus Valley Civilization, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, reachable as a day trip from Sukkur.

food_places.name: Sukkur's famous fish restaurants
food_places.specialty: Fried Indus river fish, a Sukkur specialty

transportation.notes: Short regional route, useful for Mohenjo-daro day trips
Rickshaws are common for short in-city trips

weather_info.climate_type: Hot desert climate, one of the hottest regions in Pakistan

travel_tips.tip: If visiting Mohenjo-daro, go via Larkana rather than directly, as the road connections are better maintained on that route.
Arrange a car or driver for day trips to Mohenjo-daro, since ride-hailing app coverage drops off outside the city.
Carry extra water and sun protection for summer visits given the extreme heat this region experiences.
Visit Mohenjo-daro early morning to avoid both the heat and tour crowds.

history.founded: An ancient settlement on the Indus River, with the modern city shaped heavily by British-era irrigation projects
history.city_history: Sukkur grew significantly after the British built the Sukkur Barrage in the 1930s, one of the largest irrigation systems in the world at the time, transforming the surrounding desert into fertile farmland. It also serves as the gateway to Mohenjo-daro, one of the most important archaeological sites of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
